8  Plotting

Exercise 8.1

For the countries Indonesia and Canada, create individual plots using equirectangular, orthographic, and Lambert equal area projections, while choosing projection parameters sensible for the area.

  • R
  • Python
# +proj=eqc +lat_ts=0 +lat_0=0 +lon_0=0 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +ellps=WGS84 +units=m
# +proj=ortho +lon_0=0 +lat_0=0
# +proj=laea +lon_0=0 +lat_0=0
library(sf)
# Linking to GEOS 3.14.1, GDAL 3.12.2, PROJ 9.7.1; sf_use_s2() is
# TRUE
library(tidyverse)
# ── Attaching core tidyverse packages ──────────── tidyverse 2.0.0 ──
# ✔ dplyr     1.2.1     ✔ readr     2.2.0
# ✔ forcats   1.0.1     ✔ stringr   1.6.0
# ✔ ggplot2   4.0.3     ✔ tibble    3.3.1
# ✔ lubridate 1.9.5     ✔ tidyr     1.3.2
# ✔ purrr     1.2.2
# ── Conflicts ────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ──
# ✖ dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter()
# ✖ dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()
# ℹ Use the conflicted package (<http://conflicted.r-lib.org/>) to force all conflicts to become errors
library(rnaturalearth)
ne = ne_countries(returnclass = "sf")
ne |> filter(admin == "Canada") -> ca
ne |> filter(admin == "Indonesia") -> ind
st_geometry(ca) |> st_centroid()
# Geometry set for 1 feature 
# Geometry type: POINT
# Dimension:     XY
# Bounding box:  xmin: -96.39551 ymin: 60.47676 xmax: -96.39551 ymax: 60.47676
# Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
# POINT (-96.39551 60.47676)
ca_eqc = st_crs("+proj=eqc +lat_ts=60.6")
st_geometry(ca) |> st_transform(ca_eqc) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule =TRUE)
ca_ortho = st_crs("+proj=ortho +lat_0=60.6 +lon_0=-96.4")
st_geometry(ca) |> st_transform(ca_ortho) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule=TRUE)
ca_laea = st_crs("+proj=laea +lat_0=60.6 +lon_0=-96.4")
st_geometry(ca) |> st_transform(ca_laea) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule=TRUE)
st_geometry(ind) |> st_centroid()
# Geometry set for 1 feature 
# Geometry type: POINT
# Dimension:     XY
# Bounding box:  xmin: 117.3629 ymin: -2.271715 xmax: 117.3629 ymax: -2.271715
# Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
# POINT (117.3629 -2.271715)
in_eqc = st_crs("+proj=eqc +lat_ts=-2.3")
st_geometry(ind) |> st_transform(in_eqc) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule =TRUE)
in_ortho = st_crs("+proj=ortho +lat_0=-2.3 +lon_0=117")
st_geometry(ind) |> st_transform(in_ortho) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule=TRUE)
in_laea = st_crs("+proj=laea +lat_0=-2.3 +lon_0=117")
st_geometry(ind) |> st_transform(in_laea) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule=TRUE)
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

ne = gpd.read_file("data/ne_ca_ind.gpkg")  # Natural Earth, as used by rnaturalearth
ca = ne[ne.admin == "Canada"]
ind = ne[ne.admin == "Indonesia"]

# country centres, as used for the projection parameters below
print(ca.geometry.union_all().centroid)
# POINT (-98.1423813720967 61.46907614534883)
print(ind.geometry.union_all().centroid)
# POINT (117.42340756227348 -2.221737936520538)

crs = {
    "Canada": {
        "eqc": "+proj=eqc +lat_ts=60.6",
        "ortho": "+proj=ortho +lat_0=60.6 +lon_0=-96.4",
        "laea": "+proj=laea +lat_0=60.6 +lon_0=-96.4",
    },
    "Indonesia": {
        "eqc": "+proj=eqc +lat_ts=-2.3",
        "ortho": "+proj=ortho +lat_0=-2.3 +lon_0=117",
        "laea": "+proj=laea +lat_0=-2.3 +lon_0=117",
    },
}
for name, g in [("Canada", ca), ("Indonesia", ind)]:
    for proj, p4 in crs[name].items():
        ax = g.to_crs(p4).plot(edgecolor="black", facecolor="none")
        ax.grid(True)
        ax.set_title(f"{name}: {proj}")
        plt.show()

Exercise 8.2

Recreate the plot in Figure 8.3 with ggplot2 and with tmap.

ggplot2:

  • R
  • Python
library(sf)
nc <- read_sf(system.file("gpkg/nc.gpkg", package = "sf"))
b = st_buffer(nc[1,1], units::set_units(10, km)) |> st_cast("LINESTRING")
# Warning in st_cast.sf(st_buffer(nc[1, 1], units::set_units(10,
# km)), "LINESTRING"): repeating attributes for all sub-geometries
# for which they may not be constant
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() + geom_sf(data = nc, aes(fill = BIR74)) +
        geom_sf(data = b, mapping = aes(colour = 'red')) +
        scale_fill_gradientn(colours = sf.colors())
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_map, scale_fill_cmap, theme_minimal

nc = gpd.read_file("data/nc/nc.shp")
# 10 km buffer around the first county: buffer in an azimuthal equidistant projection
first = nc.iloc[[0]]
c = first.geometry.union_all().centroid
aeqd = f"+proj=aeqd +lat_0={c.y} +lon_0={c.x}"
b = gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=first.to_crs(aeqd).buffer(10000).to_crs(nc.crs).boundary)

(
    ggplot()
    + geom_map(nc, aes(fill="BIR74"))
    + geom_map(b, color="red", fill=None)
    + scale_fill_cmap(cmap_name="Blues")
    + theme_minimal()
).show()

tmap: see https://r-tmap.github.io/tmap-book/

  • R
  • Python
library(tmap)
b = st_buffer(nc[1,1], units::set_units(10, km)) |> st_cast("LINESTRING")
# Warning in st_cast.sf(st_buffer(nc[1, 1], units::set_units(10,
# km)), "LINESTRING"): repeating attributes for all sub-geometries
# for which they may not be constant
tm_shape(nc) + 
    tm_polygons("BIR74", title = "BIR74") + 
    tm_layout(legend.outside=TRUE) +
    tm_shape(b) +
    tm_lines(legend.lwd.show = FALSE, col = 'red')
# 
# ── tmap v3 code detected ───────────────────────────────────────────
# [v3->v4] `tm_polygons()`: migrate the argument(s) related to the
# legend of the map variable `fill` namely 'title' to 'fill.legend =
# tm_legend(<HERE>)'
# [v3->v4] `tm_lines()`: use `lwd.legend = tm_legend_hide()` instead
# of `legend.lwd.show = FALSE`.
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
nc.plot(ax=ax, column="BIR74", cmap="Blues", legend=True,
        legend_kwds={"label": "BIR74", "location": "right"})
b.plot(ax=ax, color="red")
ax.set_axis_off()
plt.show()

Exercise 8.3

Recreate the plot in Figure 8.7 using the viridis colour ramp.

  • R
  • Python
library(stars)
# Loading required package: abind
library(viridis)
# Loading required package: viridisLite
r <- read_stars(system.file("tif/L7_ETMs.tif", package = "stars"))
tm_shape(r) + tm_raster(palette = viridis(100))
# 
# ── tmap v3 code detected ───────────────────────────────────────────
# [v3->v4] `tm_tm_raster()`: migrate the argument(s) related to the
# scale of the map variable `col` namely 'palette' (rename to
# 'values') to col.scale = tm_scale(<HERE>).
import rioxarray

# L7_ETMs.tif, copied from the stars R package into data/
r = rioxarray.open_rasterio("data/L7_ETMs.tif")
r.plot(col="band", col_wrap=3, cmap="viridis")
# <xarray.plot.facetgrid.FacetGrid object at 0x7fa7e7f15d30>
plt.show()

Exercise 8.4

View the interactive plot in Figure 8.7 using the “view” (interactive) mode of tmap, and explore which interactions are possible;

  • R
  • Python
library(stars)
library(viridis)
r <- read_stars(system.file("tif/L7_ETMs.tif", package = "stars"))
tmap_mode("view")
# ℹ tmap modes "plot" - "view"
# ℹ toggle with `tmap::ttm()`
tm_shape(r) + tm_raster(palette = viridis(100))
# 
# ── tmap v3 code detected ───────────────────────────────────────────
# [v3->v4] `tm_tm_raster()`: migrate the argument(s) related to the
# scale of the map variable `col` namely 'palette' (rename to
# 'values') to col.scale = tm_scale(<HERE>).
import folium
import numpy as np
from matplotlib import colormaps

# warp to lon/lat, as the web map needs
rw = r.rio.reproject("EPSG:4326")
rw = rw.where(rw != rw.rio.nodata)
xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = rw.rio.bounds()

def band_overlay(b, alpha=1.0):
    v = rw.sel(band=b).values
    v = (v - np.nanmin(v)) / (np.nanmax(v) - np.nanmin(v))
    rgba = colormaps["viridis"](v)
    rgba[np.isnan(v), 3] = 0  # transparent outside the image
    return folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay(
        rgba, bounds=[[ymin, xmin], [ymax, xmax]], opacity=alpha,
        name=f"band {b}")

m = folium.Map(location=[(ymin + ymax) / 2, (xmin + xmax) / 2], zoom_start=11)
band_overlay(1).add_to(m)
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa77465c590>
m
Make this Notebook Trusted to load map: File -> Trust Notebook

Interactions: zoom, pan, linked cursor.

Also explore adding + tm_facets(as.layers=TRUE) and try switching layers on and off.

  • R
  • Python
tmap_mode("view")
# ℹ tmap modes "plot" - "view"
tm_shape(r) + tm_raster(palette = viridis(100)) + 
        tm_facets(as.layers=TRUE)
# 
# ── tmap v3 code detected ───────────────────────────────────────────
# [v3->v4] `tm_tm_raster()`: migrate the argument(s) related to the
# scale of the map variable `col` namely 'palette' (rename to
# 'values') to col.scale = tm_scale(<HERE>).
m = folium.Map(location=[(ymin + ymax) / 2, (xmin + xmax) / 2], zoom_start=11)
for b in rw.band.values:
    band_overlay(b).add_to(m)
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa774415590>
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa7744156d0>
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa785d2a780>
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa7747b7100>
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa774400710>
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa78ef3a7a0>
folium.LayerControl().add_to(m)  # switch layers on and off
# <folium.map.LayerControl object at 0x7fa77465cec0>
m

Layer switch on left-hand side (layer symbol).

Try also setting a transparency value to 0.5.

  • R
  • Python
tmap_mode("view")
# ℹ tmap modes "plot" - "view"
tm_shape(r) + tm_raster(palette = viridis(100), alpha = .5) + 
        tm_facets(as.layers=TRUE)
# 
# ── tmap v3 code detected ───────────────────────────────────────────
# [v3->v4] `tm_tm_raster()`: migrate the argument(s) related to the
# scale of the map variable `col` namely 'palette' (rename to
# 'values') to col.scale = tm_scale(<HERE>).[v3->v4] `tm_raster()`: use `col_alpha` instead of `alpha`.
m = folium.Map(location=[(ymin + ymax) / 2, (xmin + xmax) / 2], zoom_start=11)
for b in rw.band.values:
    band_overlay(b, alpha=0.5).add_to(m)
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa774594f30>
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa77461d650>
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa77461d950>
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa7746b5130>
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa7746b5220>
# <folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay object at 0x7fa77c34d010>
folium.LayerControl().add_to(m)
# <folium.map.LayerControl object at 0x7fa774417c50>
m
